text:
**Summary:** A 12-week randomised study of 214 Queensland office workers found that sit-stand desks did not improve afternoon productivity. Task speed and accuracy were no different from those of workers with fixed desks, even though 78% of sit-stand users *felt* more productive.

The clearest benefit was less lower-back discomfort: 31% reported weekly discomfort versus 44% of the control group. Extra standing time also fell sharply, from 47 to 19 minutes a day, so the novelty fades.

**Implication:** Justify these desks on comfort and health, not productivity gains. Limitations: the test task was short, and participants knew which desk they had.
